newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares end weaker in directionless trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares end weaker in directionless trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares finished Tuesday weaker after directionless trade and dealers said indices were likely to lose more this week while the market searched for fresh factors to offer further incentive.
"It was still pretty slack but a bit more active than yesterday (Monday). The market is mixed with a softer undertone and is likely to come down a bit," one dealer said.
"It's going to be directionless this week as the market looks for news to buoy it up a bit. Trading is going to be mediocre for the rest of the week," he said.

Dealers said that the stock exchange's recent bull run and very positive sentiment meant that the market was only likely to jump on very vibrant news and that until then volumes traded would be average.
"We're unlikely to get that news this week. Volumes are not bad, but they're not great either," a dealer said.
The 57-counter industrial index lost 83.8 points to close at 10,180.82.
Industrial stocks were weighed by a 300 cent loss in Barclays which fell to 3,200 cents, a 50 cent loss in Truworths to 1,100 cents and Finhold cut 30 cents to 800 cents.
But the industrial index fell despite a 25 cent gain in Tanganda to 425 cents, a 25 cent gain in Zimplow to 625 cents, a 70 cent rise in Meikles to 100 and a 90 cent climb in J&F to 400 cents.
The seven-share mining index cut 10.75 points off its value to end the day at 1,009.87 points.
Falgold, Wankie and Alloys Mines were untraded, while Bindura lost 20 cents to 810 cents and Falcon shed 50 cents to 1,250.
